strengths: Addresses practical problem of customizing black-box frontier models without weight access, highly relevant to current deployment patterns
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse domains (reasoning and personalization) with proper baselines (GEPA, PAG) and ablations
Strong empirical results on chosen domains: 71% improvement on RuleArena Taxes, 24.6% SWE efficiency gains, near-perfect preference learning (85-100% vs 40-60%)
Novel approach: dynamic, instance-specific learned advice outperforms static prompt optimization; natural language advice is interpretable
Demonstrated transferability across model families (GPT, Gemini, Claude) and from low-cost to frontier models, enabling cost-effective optimization
Modular design prevents catastrophic forgetting on untrained tasks; comprehensive ablations (initialization, capability retention, RL comparison)
Detailed reproducibility: hyperparameters, training details, code availability, statistical reporting with 95% confidence intervals
weaknesses: Critical gap: all advisor training on low-cost models only; frontier model training missing due to cost constraints, undermining central claims. GPT-5 paradoxically underperforms GPT-4.1 mini on RuleArena (31.2% vs 64.8%), and MTOB frontier transfer shows marginal improvement (47.8 vs 46.2, p≈0.03)

Severe domain selection bias revealed by MATH-500 failure (0.668→0.682, within CI): method only works where domain knowledge gaps exist or preferences vary, limiting generalizability. No principled framework for predicting domain suitability

Small training sets create statistical power concerns: RuleArena only 75 total examples (50 train); SWE filtered to 56 examples; some results marginally significant (p≈0.03). No sample size sensitivity analysis provided

Prompt initialization dependence understated: personalization requires 'relatively strong' guidance; weak initialization learns 4× slower (5 vs 20 epochs). Practitioners must know optimization axes a priori, contradicting 'hidden preference' learning claims

Missing cost-benefit analysis: no actual API costs or compute overhead reported; 3-step architecture doubles student calls; multi-turn calls advisor every 5 steps. Cost-effectiveness claims unsupported empirically

Reward function design concerns: domain-specific functions designed by authors with no sensitivity ablation; personalization uses model judges (GPT-5 mini) as ground truth without analyzing judge bias or alignment with true preferences

Limited investigation of learned behavior: few qualitative examples; no systematic analysis of what patterns advisors discover, consistency across instances, or why curriculum learning helps some domains but not others

Architecture design choices appear ad-hoc: multiple variants (2-step, 3-step, multi-turn) with task-specific selection; 3-step costs 2× student inference but trade-offs unquantified; tool-call variant fails because models won't ask for help

Incomplete baseline comparisons: GEPA/PAG not optimized for all tasks (acknowledged but unaddressed); no empirical comparison to other learned prompt methods or simpler alternatives (in-context learning, distillation); untrained advisor sometimes severely hurts performance (52.0% from 64.8%)
Ethical considerations absent: no discussion of adversarial advice, misuse for jailbreaking, bias encoding, or safety mitigations despite interpretability claims
RL algorithm choice under-explored: uses GRPO with no ablation vs PPO/DPO; Monte Carlo variance reduction discussed but not evaluated despite high variance concerns

Scaling and generalization questions: personalization scaling only to 100 individuals; degradation in cross-family transfer (Claude Haiku: 45.1 vs GPT-4o: 47.8); all experiments on proprietary APIs limiting reproducibility

strengths: Practical approach well-suited to black-box model constraints; implementable with commercial APIs
Comprehensive multi-domain evaluation spanning specialized reasoning and personalization tasks
Demonstrates transferability of trained advisors to frontier models, reducing training cost
Clear presentation with honest discussion of limitations (Figure 10 failure case on MATH-500)
Thorough appendix with ablations on initialization, capability retention, and cross-family transfer
weaknesses: Critical concern: GPT-5 performs worse than GPT-4.1 mini on RuleArena Taxes (31.2% vs 64.8%) with no satisfactory explanation; authors state 'we do not have a clear explanation' and exclude GPT-5 from taxes, undermining experimental credibility

Fundamental limitation: method only works for out-of-distribution knowledge gaps; fails entirely on in-distribution benchmarks (MATH-500, Figure 10), severely limiting practical applicability and scope

Overstated claims: '71% improvement' misleadingly references specialized subset where cheaper model already achieved 64.8%; 'hidden preference learning' contradicted by heavy dependence on prompt initialization hints

Small-scale experiments with overfitting risk: 56-200 training examples trained for 20-40 epochs; no cross-validation, confidence intervals on training curves, or systematic investigation of generalization

Mixed transfer results diminish claims: MTOB transfer yields only 1.6-point improvement (46.2→47.8); personalization performance degrades when transferred to GPT-5 (0.889 vs 0.941), suggesting advice is model-specific not generalizable

Prompt initialization dependency for personalization: strong initialization enables 0.941 performance while weak initialization achieves only 0.749 after 5 epochs (4x slower), contradicting 'discovering' preferences when hints are provided
Incomplete baseline comparisons: GEPA not designed for multi-turn tasks; direct RL comparison only on single task; no comparison to other prompt rewriting methods or simple strong baselines

Missing critical analysis: no computational cost assessment despite multi-turn advice injection every 5 steps; no investigation into why advice generalizes across models; limited hyperparameter ablation
Robustness demonstration is weak: Figure 8 capability retention on MATH-500 is unconvincing since advisor provides zero help on this task; should demonstrate retention where advisor does help
Statistical rigor lacking: no p-values despite large error bars; no significance testing on main results; single-run evaluations with high variance across small datasets

strengths: Addresses a practical and important problem: customizing black-box frontier models without weight access
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across 6 diverse domains with strong results (71% improvement on RuleArena Taxes, 24.6% SWE efficiency gains, near-perfect preference learning)
Excellent transferability: advisors trained on low-cost models transfer effectively to frontier models, enabling cost-efficient optimization
Demonstrates robustness with no catastrophic forgetting on untrained tasks (MATH-500), important for deployed systems
Clear interpretability: before/after advice examples show advisors learn concrete, actionable guidance rather than generic text
Substantial outperformance of state-of-the-art baselines (GEPA) on specialized reasoning and personalization tasks where static methods fail
Strong reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, hardware specs, extensive ablations, and code availability provided
Well-written presentation with informative figures and comprehensive appendices covering design variants, training details, and additional experiments
weaknesses: Fundamental applicability limitation: method only works when there are knowledge gaps; fails entirely when frontier models are already knowledgeable (MATH-500), severely restricting use cases

Training-testing mismatch undermines central claims: advisors trained on low-cost models (GPT-4o mini) and tested on frontier models (GPT-5), preventing direct demonstration of frontier model improvement; authors acknowledge direct frontier training 'would be even more effective' but provide no evidence
Unexplained frontier model underperformance: GPT-5 achieves only 31.2% on RuleArena Taxes vs GPT-4.1 mini's 64.8%, raising concerns about data validity and experimental setup

Significant dependence on domain-specific prompt initialization: weak initialization requires 4× longer training (20 vs 5 epochs) and personalization tasks require guidance like 'consider review length', contradicting claims of generality
Limited technical novelty: core contribution is applying standard GRPO algorithm; no new algorithmic or methodological innovations beyond engineering
Reward function engineering required per domain (Appendix C) makes the approach less automatic and generalizable than presented

Experimental design concerns: very small datasets (RuleArena: 75 training examples; SWE: filtered to 56), domain-specific selection bias, and missing baseline comparisons (SWE efficiency vs GEPA omitted)
Modest improvements on some domains lack practical significance: MTOB transfer shows only 47.8 vs 46.2 chrF (p≈0.03), borderline statistical significance
Missing critical analysis: no computational cost assessment, limited failure mode discussion beyond MATH-500, single-task robustness validation
Generalization limitations not thoroughly explored: text-only domains, limited model family diversity (primarily Qwen advisors, GPT/Gemini students)
